newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB debenture yield jumps after downgrade news.
newsitem.headline: NCB debenture yield jumps after downgrade news.

text.p: Offer quotes for five-year bank debentures issued by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) rose sharply on Friday afternoon after Moody's Investors Service cut the bank's debenture rating, bond traders said.
NCB debentures with a 1.9 percent coupon maturing in May 1997 were being offered at six percent in the afternoon, after trading at 5.6 percent before the downgrade news, traders said.
Sell orders at six percent were worth about 2.2 billion yen, while bid orders at 6.5 percent were worth only 100 million yen, traders said.
It was the first time any NCB debenture has been quoted at the six percent level. Previously, its highest quote was 5.8 percent, traders said.
Moody's said on Friday afternoon that it had cut the rating for NCB debentures to Ba1 from Baa3 on Friday.
The downgrade of senior debt rating concludes a review started on February 18, Moody's said in a statement.
